spans.s: 1. दित, अस्, आ, अम्, cut, torn, divided.
2. दित, अस्, आ, अम्, bound; [cf. सं-दित.]

दित दित. See under rt. 3. दा at p. 408,
col. 2, and 4. दा at p. 408, col. 3.

दिति दिति, इस्, f. (fr. rt. 3. दा or दो), cut-
ting, splitting, dividing; distributing, liberality, (in
this sense also fr. rt. 1. दा); Liberality personified;
(इस्), f., N. of a divine female, (probably a N. formed
to answer to A-diti, as Sura to A-sura, and without
any distinct character: in epic poetry Diti is a
daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Kaśyapa; the race
of Daityas or implacable enemies of the gods are
described as her progeny or derived from her through
her son Hiraṇya-kaśipu; but the Viṣṇu-Purāṇa

, describes Indra as dividing the embryo in the
womb of Diti, through fear of his future enemies,
and forming the forty-nine Maruts from the divided
pieces); (इस्), m., N. of a king; a king.
—दिति-ज,
अस्, m. ‘a son of Diti,’ a Daitya, an enemy of the
gods.
—दितिजाराति (˚ज-अर्˚), इस्, m. ‘the enemy of
[]
the Daityas,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu.
—दिति-तनय
or दिति-नन्दन or दिति-सुत, अस्, m. ‘a son of
Diti,’ a Daitya.
—दिति-रूप-राक्षसी-वध, अस्,
m., N. of the twenty-first chapter of the Krīḍā-
khaṇḍa or second part of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa.
—दिति-
शोक-प्रशम, अस्, m., N. of the sixth chapter of
the Bhūmi-khaṇḍa or second part of the Padma-
Purāṇa.
—दिति-सम्बोधन, अम्, n., N. of the
ninth chapter of the Bhūmi-khaṇḍa.
दीति, इस्, f. splendor, brightness; [cf. सु-द्˚.]

दित्य, अस्, m. ‘a son of Diti,’ a Daitya; (a wrong
form for दैत्य.)

दित्यवह् दित्य-वह् or दित्य-वाह्, -वाट्, m.
(inst. दित्यौहा), दित्यौही, f. (दित्य probably a
corruption of द्वितीय), Ved. a two-year-old steer or
cow; [cf. तुर्य-वह् and दात्यौह.]

दित्सा दित्सा, f. (fr. the Desid. of rt. 1. दा),
desire or intention of giving.

दित्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, ready or wishing to give, willing
to grant (with acc.); ready to perform (e. g. श्राद्-
धम्, the funeral ceremony; cf. अ-दित्सु).

दित्स्य, अस्, आ, अम्, what one is willing to give or
ready to grant.
